Definition: from the base of G4628; dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe):--fierce, hard.
BiblicalUsage: Skleros means hard, harsh, severe, and it is the word of the man who will not yield. Paul hears it is hard to kick against the pricks, James sees fierce winds turned by a small helm, Jude hears the hard speeches of ungodly sinners, and the servant with one talent calls his lord a hard man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the hard saying is the one that exposes the heart. The servant who called his lord hard was the servant who buried his talent, and I hold that my words about God always show what I did with what He gave me.
